To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a time-frequency test can detect nonstationarity in gravitational wave detector data with high efficiency, and that this test can detect bursts with amplitudes that are about 2 times larger than those that can be detected with a test that requires prior knowledge of the statistical distribution of stationary noise.
a robust test for detecting non-stationarity in gravitational wave detector data can be constructed and the test has properties that make it suitable for use as an online monitor for stationarity.

(1) the proposed test is robust, i.e., its threshold for a specified probability of false alarm is almost independent of both the distribution and the bandwidth of the ambient stationary Gaussian noise, (2) it can detect nonstationary signals that are about 10 times larger than those that can be detected by an ideal test that assumes a priori knowledge of the distribution of the ambient stationary background noise and also its bandwidth.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of detecting gravitational wave bursts in data from interferometric gravitational wave antennas.
the detection of gravitational-wave signals from compact binary coalescence in data from the ground-based gravitational-wave detector LIGO.
the development of robust and efficient methods for the detection of gravitational-wave bursts in data from interferometric gravitational-wave detectors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the robust test is a good test to use when the noise is uncharacterized, or when the noise is characterized but the burst frequency band is unknown.
this test can be used for online monitoring of nonstationarity in gravitational wave data and can also be used to detect nonstationary bursts of gravitational waves.
the proposed robust test has a detection efficiency that is comparable to or even superior to that of the best tests that are available at the present time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed a test that is robust to the noise and is suitable for online monitoring.
the proposed robust test is a powerful and efficient method for detecting nonstationary bursts in gravitational wave detector data.
we propose a robust test to monitor stationarity of the gravitational wave detector noise.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the detection threshold for a test of stationarity can be chosen in an a priori fashion, without requiring a priori information about the nature of the noise.
the threshold of this test can be chosen in advance, without any knowledge of the noise distribution or burst frequency band.
a robust test can detect a burst at a false alarm rate of 10-5 with the same detection probability as the ideal test if the burst has an amplitude that is 3 times that of the ideal test.
